newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Koor leads Israeli mutual fund holdings.
newsitem.headline: Koor leads Israeli mutual fund holdings.

text.p: Koor Industries Ltd was the most widely held stock for the second year in a row among nine leading Israeli mutual funds at the end of 1996, Meitav Investments and Securities said on Monday.

The nine funds, which Meitav said accounted for 89 percent of all mutual fund assets, held 142 million shekels of Koor stock at the end of last year. The funds' total equities holdings were five billion shekels.
Ranked second among the top five was Israel Chemicals Ltd in which the mutual funds held 138 million shekels of equity. Meitav noted that Israel Chemicals did not rank among the top five last year.

IDB Holdings was third (136 million shekels) followed by Discount Investments (129 million shekels) and Bank Hapoalim (128 million shekels), said Meitav, an investment house that also tracks the Israeli mutual fund industry.

Meitav noted that the size of mutual fund holdings did not fully reflect fund manager preferences. It said companies with largest market capitalisations attracted proportionately more mutual fund investment.

Meitav added that not all the funds counted the top five stocks among their leading portfolio assets. Israel Chemcials was among the top five holdings in six of the nine funds and Koor was in the top five among only five.
Electra Ltd led as the company most widely held by mutual funds as a percentage of its total equity, Meitav said. The funds held 18.6 percent of Electra at the end of 1996.
Mofet Israel Technology Fund Ltd was second, followed by Feuchtwanger Industries Ltd 5, Ytong Industries Ltd and Clal Computers Ltd.
